values: Atomic and assembly modifiers are additive signed points. Positive makes harder. Negative makes easier.
Effective gameplay types = 1 / SUM(type weight share squared). One type = 1. Equal use of three types = 3.
Difficulty values are design estimates to calibrate against playtests. No automated player measurement is implied.
Blank template. L01–L03 are reserved level IDs; add your own map data, definitions and challenges.
Amber = scoring and planning inputs. Pale gray = formulas. Blue = Mental skills. Red = Physical skills. Other white cells contain editable records.
Add definitions to Atoms and Tags. Each atom has a unique ID and a signed difficulty modifier. Object, State and Parameter records remain separate.
Add a Gameplay Elements row, then Element Parts rows for its root and flattened descendants. Include each atom once. No recursive element-within-element scoring.

Keep every state in Atoms. Set Included=No for disabled states and every descendant of a disabled state. Changing State enabled alone does not rebuild an assembly; update Included or make a new assembly.
Add a Challenge Patterns row for a level, then at least two Pattern Members rows. Supply an Element ID and optional Placement ID on each. Library-only members can use a quantity.
Copy placement and element IDs from a Level view to Pattern Members. A placement can participate in multiple patterns. Never repeat it inside the same pattern.
Difficulty modifier is additive signed points: a threat may be +1.5, a player aid may be -1. A value such as range=3 remains descriptive until you assign its modifier.
Element difficulty = SUM(included atom modifier × part quantity) + assembly modifier. Element scores may be negative to represent an aid.
Raw difficulty = SUM(element difficulty × member quantity) + custom modifier. Perceived difficulty clips raw difficulty to Settings minimum/maximum, initially 0–10.
Overall difficulty = SUM(perceived challenge difficulty × level weight) / SUM(level weight). Peak is the hardest challenge. Weight initially represents relative encounter importance.
Patterns may share objects. Weights describe experienced encounters, not unique object counts. Avoid scoring the same experience twice unless repetition is intentional.
Effective gameplay types = 1 / SUM(type weight share squared). It captures both type count and balance. Every challenge has one primary gameplay type so each weight is counted once.
One row per level. Set pitch, onboarding, target, intentions and introduced element IDs. IDs introduced here are available from that level onward by design intent; placement is recorded separately.
Mental and Physical columns store comma-separated skill labels. Multiple skills are supported as text. Do not count skill tags as difficulty points.
Use chip dropdowns with Allow multiple selections. Mental options are blue and Physical options red. Native chip behavior does not round-trip to Excel; preserve text values on export.
Alien_Isolation_RLD_MISSION14.xls was used for ideas only. Its scoring values and level content were not copied. It remains unchanged.
All map geometry, scoring, pitch and onboarding content in the example is illustrative. No playtest observations, success rates or player ratings have been fabricated.
Export is not implemented in this task. The companion mapping document specifies stable IDs, snapshot selection, joins, derived geometry and designer-owned fields.
Current Workshop playtests are private temporary copies and are discarded on return to Edit. A future export must explicitly capture the playtest copy before it is discarded.

Rows 6–85 support 80 records per catalog or mapping. Copy the final formula row down and extend every referenced range and validation if you exceed row 85. A future exporter should size ranges to the snapshot.

The first three level views have 25 placement and 25 challenge slots each. Totals include all records. Duplicate a Level view and set B4 to a registered Level ID for more levels. Extend slots if its listed/total counters differ.
Missing modifiers, members or invalid IDs block downstream scores. Blank means no record. Zero is an intentional numeric score. Resolve Readiness messages before interpreting outputs.

Update records by stable ID. Keep scoring, skill tags, pitch, onboarding and intentions when refreshing Workshop content. Mark deleted source records for review if designer mappings still reference them.
